title: Learning Mechanisms Explaining Learning With Digital Tools in Educational Settings: a Cognitive Process Framework
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a core problem in research on educational technology: digital tools often show positive effects on learning, but the mechanisms explaining those effects are not always specified. The authors argue that it is insufficient to study only whether digital tools improve outcomes; researchers also need to identify the cognitive processes and learning activities through which specific digitally enriched instructional features influence learning.

To address this, the paper proposes the CoDiL framework (Cognitive process framework on the Learning mechanisms of Digital tools in educational settings), which integrates ideas from the knowledge-learning-instruction (KLI) framework, the SOI model (selection-organization-integration), and utilization-of-learning-opportunity (ULO) frameworks. The framework distinguishes between digital instructional features, the learning activities they may stimulate, the underlying cognitive processes, and the resulting knowledge acquisition. It highlights content-specific learning activities such as exploration, self-explanation, refinement, revision, conducting experiments, and formulating hypotheses, and links these to features like adaptive feedback, prompting, simulations, and contrasting cases.

The paper is conceptual rather than an empirical intervention study, so it does not focus on a particular student sample, grade level, or classroom implementation. Instead, it uses examples from mathematics and science learning to illustrate how the framework could guide the design and evaluation of digital tools. The main conclusion is that future research on digital learning should specify knowledge components, identify the learning activities needed to acquire them, design instructional features to stimulate those activities, and collect process data to validate the link between student-tool interaction and cognition.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed conceptual review/framework paper, not an empirical study evaluating an intervention or reporting original outcome data. It does not provide a testable design with sample, measures, or effect estimates for K-12 learning outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct measured impact on learner outcomes; it proposes a theoretical framework (CoDiL) for studying digital tools in education. Any implications for science learning are indirect and not evidenced with effect sizes or outcome data in this article.
